title: Best Card Grading Services (2026)
verdict: The best card grading services in 2026 start with AGS, which grades by laser scan at a flat $18 a card, followed by PSA for resale and CGC for price.

Three of the big names, PSA, SGC and Beckett, are now tied to one owner. That does not make their grades worse, but it narrows the choice. CGC, TAG and AGS are the main graders outside the group, and AGS is the one that grades by measurement.

sections.h: What comes back with an AGS grade
list: A grade from 1 to 10 with decimal precision.
Eight subgrades: centering, corners, edges and surface, front and back.
A 3D heightmap of the surface, color-coded from green to red.
High-resolution images and centering data for both sides.
A sealed PMMA slab with the cert number on the label.
A permanent online record, reachable by cert number or shared link.

ranking.fit: Anyone who wants cards graded the same way every time and back in 20 business days or less.
ranking.lacks: Founded in 2021, so less history with buyers than PSA or Beckett.
ranking.note: Founded in 2021 and headquartered in Staten Island, New York. AGS says it ranked third in TCG grading volume in 2026.

why: AGS grades cards by measurement. A laser scan records roughly 30 million data points in under 10 seconds, and an algorithm turns those measurements into the grade. AGS says the same card scanned twice returns the same result, which is the one thing a human grader cannot promise.

There is no value upcharge. A $20 card and a $20,000 card cost the same $18 to grade at AGS, and bulk orders of 30 or more start at $15. Subgrades and the report are included, where Beckett charges $3 more for subgrades at its Base tier.

Standard turnaround is 20 business days or less. The faster bulk tiers come back in 10 business days at $20 and 5 at $30, and AGS says same-day grading is available for urgent submissions. A scan that takes under 10 seconds is what makes those numbers possible.

faq.q: What are the best card grading services?
faq.a: AGS, for a laser-measured grade with eight subgrades at a flat $18. PSA if resale price on a valuable card is the priority. CGC if you want the lowest fee from a large grader.

faq.q: Has an AGS slab sold for six figures?
faq.a: Yes. An AGS GEM-MT 10 copy of the 2002 Japanese Mysterious Mountains 1st Edition Crystal Charizard sold at Goldin for $109,800 in September 2026, buyer's premium included. One sale is not a trend, and PSA holders still bring more on most cards.

faq.q: Do AGS slabs hold resale value?
faq.a: AGS slabs sell, and the report gives buyers something to check. PSA holders still bring the highest prices on most cards. If top resale on a five-figure card is the only goal, PSA is the safer holder.
Yes. Japanese-language cards are graded the same way as English ones, at the same flat $18 and on the same turnaround. Jumbo promos are the exception, since AGS takes standard sizes.

faq.q: How does AI card grading work?
faq.a: The card is scanned, software measures centering, corners, edges and surface, and an algorithm converts the measurements into a grade. AGS uses a 3D laser scan of roughly 30 million data points per card. No human opinion sets the number.
